Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:10:1.hebrew: דבר מהדר הוא - ממתנה זו. אם חזר בו, לאחר שיצאו שני שטרות בב"ד, יזכה האחרון:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:10:1.english: He is capable of retracting - from this gift. If he retracted, after two deeds are produced in court, the last [recipient] acquires [the property].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:10:2.hebrew: א"נ יהבה - שוב לאיניש אחרינא במתנת בריא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:10:2.english: Even if he gave it - subsequently to another person as a gift of a healthy person.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:10:3.english: There is no loss to him - [Namely,] to that latter [recipient], through this document that we are returning to this [first one].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:12:2.hebrew: דהוא קדים - שיהא שטרו קודם, דכיון דמת אביו מחליו, זכה משנתנה לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:12:2.english: For he is prior - That his deed is earlier, for since his father died from his illness, he acquired [the property] from when it was given to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:12:3.english: And I will divide [it] with him - I will divide [it] with him in this conspiracy.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:14:1.hebrew: קמא זכה - מאחר ששני השטרות יצאו משמך, הקודם זכה, שמתנת בריא הם. והשתא דאוקימנא טעמא דלא יחזיר משום דלמא כתבה להאי ואמליך ולא יהבה ליה והדר כתבה לאיניש אחרינא, ליכא למרמי אמתנות, ולא תידוק מתני' גבי מתנות "הא אמר תנו, נותנין"; דכי נמי אמר תנו, שייך למימר טעמא דלא יחזיר משום "שאני אומר כתובין היו ונמלך עליהן שלא לתנן", והדר כתבה לאיניש אחרינא. וגבי דייתקאות, ע"כ אם אמר תנו — נותנין, אם הוא קיים; דהא תלה תנא דידן טעמא משום "שאני אומר נמלך עליהן שלא לתנן", ואי נמי הכי הוה דנמלך, השתא אם אמר תנו — נותנין, דליכא למיחש למידי. וה"ק: מצא דייתיקי או מתנה — לא יחזיר, שאני אומר כו'. והיכא דאמר תנו, שייך למימר לא יחזיר משום טעמא ד"שאני אומר" — כגון מתנת בריא, או בשכיב מרע ומת ובריה קאמר תנו — שמעי' ממתני' דלא יחזיר, ולא דייקינן "האמר תנו, נותנין". והיכא דלא שייך למימר "שאני אומר" — כגון בשכיב מרע שלא מת מחליו — דייקינן "האמר תנו", דבטל "שאני אומר", הלכך נותנין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:14:1.english: The first one acquires [it] - Since both deeds were issued under your name, the earlier one acquires [the property], as they are a gift of a healthy person. And now that we have established the reason for "he shall not return [it]" as being because perhaps he wrote it for this person, and reconsidered and did not give it to him, and then wrote it for another person, there is no [contradiction] to raise regarding gifts, and do not infer from the Mishnah regarding gifts: "If he said 'give [it],' they give [it]." For even when he said "give [it]," it is applicable to state the reason for "he shall not return [it]" as "for I say they were written and he reconsidered regarding them not to give them," and then wrote it for another person. And regarding wills, perforce if he said "give [it]," they give [it], if he is alive; for our Tanna made the reason dependent on "for I say he reconsidered regarding them not to give them," and even if it were so that he reconsidered, now if he said "give [it]," they give [it], since there is nothing to be concerned about. And this is what [the Mishnah] is saying: If one found a will or a gift — he shall not return [it], "for I say, etc." And where he said "give [it]," [and] it is applicable to say "he shall not return [it]" because of the reason of "for I say" — such as a gift of a healthy person, or in [the case of] a deathbed person who died and his son says "give [it]" — we learn from the Mishnah that he shall not return [it], and we do not infer "if he said 'give [it],' they give [it]." And where it is not applicable to say "for I say" — such as in [the case of] a deathbed person who did not die from his illness — we infer "if he said 'give [it],'" for "for I say" is nullified; therefore, they give [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:15:1.english: [If one] found a receipt - [A receipt] that a wife wrote to her husband, "I have received my marriage contract [payment]," while she is still married to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:16:1.english: And she did not give [it] until Tishrei - And he did not pay until Tishrei.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:16:2.english: And she went - She [did so] while she was still under him [i.e., married to him], between Nisan and Tishrei.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:16:3.english: And she sold her marriage contract - To another [person].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:16:4.hebrew: בטובת הנאה - כלומר בזול, לפי שנותן מעותיו בספק, שאם תמות היא, יירשנה בעלה ויפסיד מי שלקחה, ואם ימות בעלה או יגרשנה, יהיה לוקח במקומה ויגבה כתובתה. ושוב לא היה לבעלה לפרוע לה הכתובה אלא ללוקח, ושובר שנכתב בשמה אינו כלום:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:16:4.english: For financial advantage - That is to say, cheaply, because [the buyer] gives his money subject to uncertainty: for if she dies, her husband will inherit her and the one who bought it will lose [his money], and if her husband dies or divorces her, the buyer will stand in her place and collect her ketubah. And [thus] her husband no longer had to pay the ketubah to her, but rather to the buyer, and a receipt written in her name is nothing.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:17:1.hebrew: ומפיק לשובר - שכתוב בניסן, ויקדום לשטרו של לוקח, ויחזיק הבעל בקרקע המיוחדת לכתובתה שלא כדין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:17:1.english: And he produces the receipt - Which is written in Nisan, and it will precede the purchaser's deed, and the husband will take possession of the land designated for her marriage contract unlawfully.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:1:1.hebrew: הא בבריא - שהיה שטר מתנת בריא, דלא כתיב ביה כדקציר ורמי בערסיה, כדין שכותבין בשטרי מתנות שכיב מרע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:1:1.english: This [refers to] a healthy person - For it was a deed of a gift of a healthy person, in which it is not written "while he was ill and lying in his bed," as is the rule that they write in deeds of gifts of a person on his deathbed.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:2:1.hebrew: דבר מהדר הוא - שיכול לחזור במתנתו. אם כתב שני שטרות, השני זוכה, שהרי חזר בו מראשון:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:2:1.english: Who is capable of retracting - For he can retract his gift. If he wrote two deeds, the second [recipient] acquires [it], for he has retracted from the first.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:4:1.english: If he gave it to him as the gift of a healthy person - To that latter [recipient].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:4:2.english: He has no loss - Through this deed that is returned to this [first recipient].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:6:1.hebrew: בבריא - כגון שהיה השטר זה הנמצא מתנת בריא, שהוא זכה לשטר המאוחר לו, שאינו יכול לחזור במתנתו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:6:1.english: In [the case of] a healthy person - For example, where this found deed was a gift of a healthy person, which prevails over a deed [dated] later than it, since [the donor] cannot retract his gift.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:8:1.hebrew: דאי יהבתיה לאיניש אחרינא לית ליה פסידא - בשטרא דכתבת השתא, דמאן דקדים שטריה זכה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:8:1.english: So that if you gave it to another person, he will have no loss - through the document that you write now, because the one whose document is earlier acquires [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:8:2.english: [He retracts] from it - [This is a case] where he [the giver] is still alive and said, "Give [it] to this one."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:9:1.hebrew: הא בבריה - שמת מחליו, וזה בנו אומר החזירהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 19b:9:1.english: That [refers] to his son - That he died from his illness, and this [is where] his son says, "Return it."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 19b:12:1.hebrew: ובתר אבוה כתבה איהו לאיניש אחרינא - תימה: אמאי לא אמרינן נמי שנתנה האב תחלה במתנת שכיב מרע, ואח"כ האב עצמו כתבה להאי ולא יהבה ליה, ומת האב ונתקיימה המתנה לראשון, והבן רוצה שתהיה לשני:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 19b:12:1.english: And after his father [died], he wrote it to another person - [This is] astonishing: why do we not also say that the father initially gave it as a deathbed gift, and afterwards the father himself wrote it for this [person] and did not give it to him, and the father died, so the gift was upheld for the first [recipient], while the son wants it to belong to the second [person]?

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 19b:15:1.hebrew: מצא שובר כו' וליחוש דלמא כתב ליתן בניסן כו' - וא"ת: לפרוך על מתני' דגט פשוט (ב"ב דף קסז.), דכותבין שובר לאשה? וכ"ת לא חיישינן אלא היכא שנפל ואתרע — הא פריך לעיל (בבא מציעא יב:) גבי כותבין שטר ללוה, אע"ג דליכא ריעותא! וי"ל דמצי לדחויי בשטרי הקנאה. אבל הכא, אי בשטרי הקנאה מיירי — כי אין האשה מודה נמי יחזיר לבעל! ד"אין אשה מודה" משמע אפילו אינה אומרת שהוא מזויף, אלא אומרת שכתבה ליתן ולא נתנה, ואומרת עתה "אל תתנו", לפי שנמלכה — דומיא ד"מצא שוברין" דמתניתין, ד"לא יחזיר, שאני אומר כתובים היו ונמלך כו'":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 19b:15:1.english: "If one found a receipt, etc. — But let us suspect that perhaps [she] wrote [it] to give in Nisan, etc." - And if you will ask: Let [the Gemara] raise a difficulty against the Mishnah in Get Pashut (Bava Batra 167a), [which states] that one may write a receipt for a woman! And if you will say [that] we only suspect [this] where it fell and was weakened [in credibility] — behold, [the Gemara] raised a difficulty earlier (Bava Metzia 12b) regarding [the rule that] one may write a [loan] document for a borrower, even though there is no weakening [of credibility]! And one can answer that [there] it could deflect [the difficulty by saying that the Mishnah is speaking] of documents of acquisition (shitrei hakna'ah). However, here, if [the baraita] is speaking of shitrei hakna'ah, [then] even when the wife does not admit [it], he should also return [it] to the husband! For "the wife does not admit" implies even [a case where] she does not say that it is forged, rather she says that she wrote [it] to give [to him] and did not give [it], and she says now, "Do not give [it to him]," because she changed her mind — similar to "If one found receipts" in our Mishnah, where [the ruling is that] "he should not return [them], for I say they were written and he changed his mind, etc."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 19b:6:1.hebrew: ברייתא בבריא דלמא כתבה להאי ולא יהביה ליה - היינו דלא כאביי, דלדידיה אמאי לא נהדר כיון שהוא רוצה? דעדיו בחתומיו זכין לו היכא דמטא שטרא לידיה. ואביי יתרץ כדרב זביד דבסמוך:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 19b:6:1.english: The baraita [is referring to] a healthy person; perhaps he wrote it for this one and did not give it to him - This is not in accordance with Abaye, for according to him, why should we not return [it] since he wants [to give it]? For [Abaye holds that] its witnesses, by their signatures, acquire [it] for him once the deed reaches his hand. And Abaye will resolve [the baraita] in accordance with Rav Zevid [just] below:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 19b:9:1.hebrew: והא אידי ואידי דייתיקאות קתני - וא"ת: ולפרוך נמי "והא מתנות קתני"! ואור"ת דמיירי מתני' שפירש שנותן לו גוף ופירי מהיום אם לא יחזור עד לאחר מיתה, דמצי הדר ביה. ורש"י דחק לפרש דגבי מתנות אפי' אם אמר "תנו" אין נותנין, וה"פ דמתניתין: "שאני אומר כתובין היו ונמלך עליהם שלא ליתנן", ויהיב לאיניש אחרינא, ועתה רוצה לחזור בו מן השני וליתנה לראשון; לפיכך אפילו אם אמר "תנו" אין נותנין. אבל דייתיקי — אם אמר "תנו" נותנין, דאפילו נמלך ונתן לאחר יכול לחזור. וקשה לפירושו, דא"כ פירוש ד"נמלך" דמתני' יהיה בשני עניינים! ותו: לעיל גבי גט, דדייק "הא אמר תנו נותנין" אפילו לזמן מרובה, לפרש"י ז"ל מנ"ל לפרושי הכי? דלמא ה"פ: משום דנמלך איכא למיחש שמא לא ניתן הגט עדיין, ולכך אפילו אם אמר "תנו" אין נותנין! אלא לשון "ונמלך" משמע שעתה אינו רוצה, כדפרישית לעיל (בבא מציעא י"ח. ד"ה הא):
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 19b:9:1.english: "But doesn't both this and that teach [about] wills?" - And if you ask: Let [the Gemara] also object, "But doesn't it teach [about] gifts?" And Rabbeinu Tam answers that the Mishnah is dealing [with a case] where he specified that he is giving him the principal and the produce from today, provided he does not retract until after death, so that he is able to retract. And Rashi forced himself to explain that regarding gifts, even if he said "Give [it]," we do not give [it], and this is the explanation of the Mishnah [according to Rashi]: "For I say they were written and he reconsidered regarding them not to give them," and he gave [it] to another person, and now he wants to retract from the second [recipient] and give it to the first; therefore, even if he said "Give [it]," we do not give [it]. However, [regarding] a sickbed will (deitiki) — if he said "Give [it]," we do give [it], for even if he reconsidered and gave [it] to another, he can retract. And this is difficult according to his explanation, for if so, the meaning of "he reconsidered" in the Mishnah would have two [different] senses! And furthermore: above, regarding a bill of divorce (get), where [the Gemara] infers, "If he said 'Give [it],' we give [it]," even after a long time — according to the explanation of Rashi, of blessed memory, from where does he know to explain it thus? Perhaps this is its explanation: because he reconsidered, there is reason to be concerned that perhaps the get was not yet given, and therefore even if he said "Give [it]," we do not give [it]! Rather, the expression "and he reconsidered" implies that now he does not want [to give it], as I explained above (Bava Metzia 18a, s.v. Ha).
